title: Minimum Generations to Target Point
summary: Given a 2D integer array points where each point is represented as [xi, yi, zi] in 3D space, and an integer array target representing a target point, define generation 0 as the initial list of points.
statement: Given a 2D integer array points where each point is represented as [xi, yi, zi] in 3D space, and an integer array target representing a target point, define generation 0 as the initial list of points. For each integer k >= 1, form generation k by considering every pair of two distinct points from all points in generations 0 through k-1. For each pair of points a = [x1, y1, z1] and b = [x2, y2, z2], compute a new point c = [floor((x1 + x2) / 2), floor((y1 + y2) / 2), floor((z1 + z2) / 2)] and include c in generation k. All points in generation k are formed simultaneously from points in generations 0 through k-1. After generation k is formed, the points in generation k are available for forming later generations. Return the smallest integer k such that the target point appears in one of the generations 0 through k. If the target is already in the initial points, return 0. If it is impossible to obtain the target through this process, return -1. Note: The floor function rounds down to the nearest integer. "Two distinct points" means the points must have different (x, y, z) coordinates; a point cannot be paired with itself, and pairing two points with identical coordinates is not allowed.
constraints: points contains 1–20 distinct 3D integer points with coordinates 0–6; target has the same bounds.
Each generation simultaneously adds coordinate-wise floored midpoints of every pair of distinct known points.
Return the first generation containing target, or -1 when closure stops growing.
hints: The coordinate bounds limit the closure to at most 343 distinct points.
Maintain all known points and generate every pair midpoint in synchronous rounds.
Remove points already known; if no new point appears, the target is impossible.
Round batching matches generation semantics, and finite closure guarantees termination.
editorial: Round batching matches generation semantics, and finite closure guarantees termination.

tests.explanation: The two initial points produce target [3,3,3] in generation one.
Generation one adds [2,2,2], which pairs with zero to add target in generation two.
